subject: Data handling boundaries and reduced-log pilot — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morris <lena.morris@neurovistahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Data handling boundaries and reduced-log pilot — recap & next steps

Hi Lena — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap of what I heard and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of asks from NeuroVista security
- No persistent storage of patient-identifiable information (PHI/PII) in hosted logs.
- If transcripts are retained for debugging, TTL must be <= 24 hours and be configurable per environment.
- KV cache and model context must be resident in EU for production.
- Audit trail (who/when) required for any access to logs or debug dumps.
- SOC 2 + encryption-in-transit & at-rest; support for customer-managed KMS preferred.

What we suggested on the call
- Short-term: a reduced-log pilot (non-production) where we can run 1) masked inputs, 2) ephemeral KV caches with custom TTL, or 3) a strict 0-retention mode (no model input logs persisted beyond transient processing).
- Mid-term: Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed KMS and EU residency option for production workload.

Open questions we need from you to scope engineering work
1) Are there any regulatory reasons NeuroVista cannot accept TTL up to 24 hours for debug artifacts (vs true 0-retention)?
2) Do you need field-level redaction rules (we can provide client-side SDK helpers) or is token-level hashing acceptable?
3) Which EU region do you need residency in (e.g., eu-west-1 vs eu-central-1)?
4) Will your procurement team require a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and a subprocessor list before any pilot?

Next steps / actions
- I'll share a short PDF with three options (0-retain, 24h debug window, 7d limited logs) and the tradeoffs — attached.
- Please send over the security questionnaire you filled out during the call (attach if possible) so we can map controls directly.
- Marissa (CS lead) will follow up on the pilot timeline and SOW once we confirm the option.

If you’re comfortable with that plan, I’ll loop in engineering for a feasibility note and an ETA for a pilot runbook.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

From: Lena Morris <lena.morris@neurovistahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: NeuroVista Security Team <security@neurovistahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 17:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Data handling boundaries and reduced-log pilot — recap & next steps

Karthik — thanks for the summary and for being explicit. A few clarifications from our side: we’re security/compliance-first given the regulated workflows. Answers inline below.

1) TTL window: we prefer true 0-retention for production inference. For pilot and debugging we will accept up to 24 hours only if data is encrypted with keys we control and we have a documented purge/justification process.

2) Redaction: client-side field-level redaction is our standard. We need a way to validate redaction (hash + salt verification) before data leaves our environment. Token-level hashing alone is not sufficient for PHI.

3) Residency: eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) is preferred for anything production-facing. Pilot can run in eu-west-1 if needed.

4) DPA & subprocessors: yes — procurement requires an executed DPA and subprocessor disclosure prior to any pilot with production data. We can do a limited pilot with synthetic or de-identified data while legal executes paperwork.

Attached is the security questionnaire (filled). I also attached NeuroVista’s minimum security controls matrix — it highlights the KMS and audit requirements.

From a risk perspective, the path we prefer: private control plane + customer-managed keys + ephemeral model inputs (0-retention) in production. If Redwood can’t offer that today, we may evaluate a short-term pilot but will not move production traffic without the controls above.

Best,
Lena

--
Lena Morris
Head of Security & Compliance | NeuroVista Health
lena.morris@neurovistahealth.com | +44 20 7000 1122
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morris <lena.morris@neurovistahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data handling boundaries and reduced-log pilot — recap & next steps

Lena — appreciate the clear constraints — that helps a lot. Short answers and concrete options below.

Feasibility summary (high-level)
- 0-retention in production: feasible with Redwood Private (customer VPC) + customer-managed KMS + strict pipeline that disables event and model input persistence. We will need 2–3 weeks for infra packaging and checklisting, and another 2–4 weeks for security review and SOC evidence exchange.

- Pilot debugging (24h TTL) with customer KMS: feasible on hosted dedicated capacity. We can enable an encrypted short retention bucket accessible only via an audit-gated flow. We’ll provide a proof-of-privacy runbook.

- Field-level redaction: we have two approaches — 1) SDK-side field redactors (recommended) that run before data is sent, and 2) platform transformers that apply regex/token policies. SDK approach gives you verifiable pre-send hashing plus a signed verification header.

Technical tradeoffs (brief)
- 0-retention means losing any post-request debugging artifacts; operationally we provide higher-fidelity observability hooks (tracing IDs) without plaintext content.
- Encrypted 24h window gives faster incident triage but increases blast radius; customer-managed keys mitigate that.

Attachments: I attached a short options doc that maps each mode to the required contractual controls and a draft SOW for a 4-week pilot.

Recommended next steps
1) Redwood to provide SOC 2 + subprocessor list and DPA template (I’ll attach in a follow-up).
2) NeuroVista to confirm whether we start with a synthetic-data pilot (preferred) or request limited production pilot under strict controls.
3) If pilot: Marissa to propose a project timeline and a one-page runbook for the pilot by EOD Wednesday.

I’ll loop in engineering (Aditya) to validate the 2–3 week infra packaging estimate once you confirm the pilot type.

Thanks — Karthik
